Goldfinger

By: Graham Coetzer | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A new kind of randlord has emerged of Joburg's East rand, buying up illegally mined gold in an elaborate scam that's costing the country billions.

Summary:
Carte Blanche has done numerous stories about zamazamas and the illegal gold trade - it's costing the country in lives lost, violence in communities and gold stolen from legitimate mining operations. But what's fuelling this dangerous trade? Our investigation uncovers a complex gold scam that launders illegal gold while at the same time generating bogus VAT claims, resulting in billions of rands being stolen from SARS every year. We reveal how the scam works and who is profiting from the trade.

Further information:
A small loophole exists in the Second Hand Goods Act - all gold nuggets, ingots, bars and coins are zero-rated but gold jewellery isn't. It's this loophole that is fuelling the violent and dangerous illegal gold trade. Illegal gold traders on the ground are willing to pay over the world market price for gold. This creates an incentive to steal gold from legitimate mines, to mine gold illegally and to smuggle tonnes of gold into South Africa illegally. Once the gold is in South Africa it's sold on through a complex web of traders and refineries. Along the way the gold is melted down with other alloys to change what was pure gold into what looks strikingly similar to melted down jewellery. Paperwork is then forged to make it appear as if the gold did in fact come from second-hand jewellery buyers. With the gold disguised with other metals and with the correct paperwork the gold looks perfectly legitimate and is then sold on to the likes of Rand Refinery, local banks or exported. The end buyer has no idea that the gold they're buying may have been mined in dangerous underground illegal mines in South Africa, Zimbabwe, Angola or the DRC.
We have three sources who agreed to interviews with their identities hidden - these sources have all been part of this illegal trade at one point or another. We have confirmed everything they have told us with members of the SARS task team on precious metals and with the Hawks. We have also been given Rand Refinery's internal figures for scrap gold purchases and Krugerrand sales which clearly demonstrate the extent of the problem.
We also have undercover footage of illegal mining operations in Zimbabwe including two deaths that occurred on these mines.
We also recorded phonecalls where we discussed doing an illegal gold deal with the principal of a high school in Springs. He specifically named his buyer - Buks Jansen. We believe we have enough evidence to implicate Buks as one of the major kingpins behind the illegal gold trade. We believe that through the refinery he used to own, Dedrego Trading, that he made false VAT claims fromnginto hundreds of millions of rands.

• Payment system between Zim and SA for goods a bit confusing. Could cut this too.
• VAT scam bit to be made clearer. Perhaps use examples with actual figures
• Who are people doing fake invoices? Add dramatisation.
• Merran thought you should make the distinction between how little the zamas make vs the rest of the people in the gold chain (funny that).
• E-toll upsund repeated at end again
• Ghost voices of insiders to change – seems like it’s all the same person. One needs to be a woman where we can see Susan.
• Hidden camera of school principal confusing. Use other visuals of him

Legal comments as per Dario:
• Shots of people mining and grinding. Maybe blur their faces.
• Do all the sources implicate Buks Jansen – 3 sources and SARS?
• Did we ask if we could speak to Buks himself when phoning his wife? Maybe include more of wife declining interview and not being prepared to give an email address.
• School principal – is this a fair extract of what he said in response. Double check.
• Change script: The Jansens are not the only people ALLEGED to be involved in this
• Buks open Facebook profile photos. Need to credit. Source: Facebook
Including the Rand Refinery – the legal perspective:
Including figures without expert analysis is legally very risky. Rethink this after an anlyst has looked at this. Could rather include comment from Adrian Lackay about Rand Refinery. If this is included Dario would need to see again.

George feedback 2/9/2014
He said it’s really good
Doesn’t have many issues.
George thinks that it should stay at 19 minutes
He thinks that sources’ voices ALL need to be chironed otherwise we can’t hear what they are saying because of the distortio. You need to find a woman for Susan’s voice and also chiron.
Very glad you got Buks’ wife
The only thing that worried him in principal is aren’t we telling criminals exactly how to do the scam... we haven’t left any steps out – that is a huge ethical problem. He wanted to know whether you have left any steps out or whether there are any steps that can be left out.

VIEWING 2 SEPTEMBER 2
Their attempts to stem the tide ‘is’ made more difficult should be ‘are’ made

• When you talk about how Rand issued a letter saying jewellery has to come in its original form he says ‘We didn’t seem much jewellery we declare it but didn’t see it. not sure what that means’
• Do we have Rand Refinery’s full comment in the story? Where they say that the letter is speculative etc we haven’t given full context there or their full right of reply... we havetn put in them saying that their letter was not in response to SARS.
• Is it right to include them if we don’t have much against them? Very worried that we are using them and that a reasonable viewer will think that they are hiding something and part of a scam and hiding something.
• Remove them from a legal point of view that is what we decided
• Add in in script what happens to the gold – it goes to large refiners who buy it unwittingly, exported etc
• Fonts looked wrong on your straps on goldfinger story – will you double check tool kit – shouldn’t be bold throughout etc

Press Release:


Goldfinger
In 1886 gold was discovered in Johannesburg, setting off a massive gold rush. More than a hundred years later, it would seem that very little has changed in the City of Gold. A new kind of randlord has emerged, dealing in gold on the black market. An ingenious scam that’s costing the country billions. Carte Blanche gets down to unearthing the facts.


Script:


FINAL SCRIPT: Goldfinger

Date: 14 September 2014
Producer: Graham Coetzer
Journalist: Susan Comrie
Presenter: Devi Sankaree Govender

Source 2 (Actor’s Voice / Identity Protected): You’re never going to stop the gold coming into the country – that we need to make peace with.

Captain Paul Ramaloko (Hawks: Spokesperson): We are talking about serious money-laundering where millions are involved.

Adrian Lackay (SARS: Spokesperson): They feed off the proceeds of crime, they literally partake in a system that sends poor, desperate people underground to illegally mine gold.

Source 2: Teachers are doing gold deals on the school grounds, headmasters are becoming gold traders.

Source 3 (Actor’s Voice / Identity Protected): And they’re portraying it like they’re this Christian people that does everything right.

Source 1 (Actor’s Voice / Identity Protected): I was making ten million rand a month, by doing a thousand kilos a month, I was one of the biggest.

Devi Sankaree Govender: This is Johannesburg’s East Rand, once one of the richest mining areas in the country. Although most of the mines have closed down, a new kind of “randlord” has emerged, buying up gold on the black market in an ingenious scam netting billions.

This is Buks Jansen, a former cop from Springs who claims to have become an overnight millionaire by winning the lottery. But according to our sources he’s alleged to be one of the big five South African players in the illicit gold trade.

Source 1: At the moment I would say Buks Jansen is one of the biggest guys left in the industry currently.

This is Dedrego, a gold refinery in Springs that used to be run by Buks Jansen , although the company was registered in his wife Cornelia’s name. According to documents leaked to Carte Blanche, Dedrego did a turnover of R4 billion in 2011 and even considered taking a R100-million loan in order to finance more gold purchases. It is alleged that illegitimate as well as legitimate gold was refined here.

Source 2: Everyone knows exactly what the Jansens are doing. But so many people is dependent on them that they just look the other way.

Buks' alleged involvement in gold trading is part of a much wider network of organised crime syndicates involved in the illegal gold trade. It’s a sinister world where we are told that life is cheap and cash is king.

Source 1: Even if I spend R10 million a month on security that will not be enough to protect me from the people involved in this industry.

And here’s the big secret they’re all trying to protect – the illicit gold trade really has very little to do with the value of gold. The truth is the underground world of gold smuggling is actually fuelled by a massive VAT scam .

Source 2: It’s just if you mine gold there’s no VAT to it, it’s a zero-rated item. The moment you sell second-hand gold jewellery, there’s a VAT to it

It’s a complicated scam – but here’s a simplified example of how it works:
• Step 1: The syndicates buy a R100 worth of illegal gold. Because it’s an illegal deal, they haven’t paid VAT on the R100.
• Step 2: They employ an elaborate scheme to legitimise the illegal gold by claiming it comes from second-hand gold jewellery.
• Step 3: Now they can sell the so-called legit gold again for a R100, but because they’re selling it through a registered VAT vendor, they are charging R114. Magically creating R14 profit.

Source 2: According to government I have paid VAT therefore by law I’m allowed to get it back. In this case I never paid VAT I’m just purely stealing money out of the coffers of government.

To really understand this scam we need to start at step 1, on the ground in Springs, a modern day gold boom town where syndicates are buying as much illegal gold as they can get their hands on.

Devi Sankaree Govender: They’re called zamazamas which in isiZulu means “to try for just a little bit”. And that’s precisely what illegal miners in this area are doing – travelling down dangerous shafts and braving armed gunmen to get just a little bit of gold to sell on the black market.

Chris Zulu: The zamazamas there is nothing more which they can do. They are looking for a job, they can’t find a job. They thought this is much better, where can they find something to eat, than to go to someone’s house and to go and break.

This is Chris Zulu, he provides protection to a group of local zamazamas.

Chris Zulu: Because there is a lot of fighting in these illegal minings. Shooting, killing each other.

The mines in this area have all been closed and the shafts sealed, but illegal miners have found ways in. Contrary to popular belief, most zamazamas aren’t the people making the big money off illegal gold.

Kenneth Dlamini (Sector 8 Community Policing Forum): Those zamazamas guys who go underground, they are only making something that they can live with.

Kenneth Dlamini is a member of the Sector 8 Community Policing Forum but he also lives in Lindelani outside Springs, alongside many of the people involved in illegal mining.

Kenneth Dlamini (Sector 8 Community Policing Forum): The bases here in Lindelani, there could be 20 to 30 bases, where they process their sand from the ground, because they go to different bases.

The zamazamas we met were all Zimbabwean. They travel underground, about a kilometer down an abandoned ventilation shaft, where the zamazamas will often spend days mining in pitch darkness before returning to the surface. Once the gold has been brought to the surface, it’s taken to one of the many bases where the gold-bearing material is crushed and processed.

Kenneth Dlamini (Sector 8 Community Policing Forum): They carry this bag from underground. They get it out like this.

The material goes through two crushing processes, all done by hand.

Kenneth Dlamini (Sector 8 Community Policing Forum): And after that, when it’s fine, they take it to the roller.

The roller, or phenduka, is filled with steel ball-bearings and a mixture of water, mercury and cleaning detergents to get the mined material as fine as possible.

Kenneth Dlamini (Sector 8 Community Policing Forum): The shiny thing it’s gold.

The tiny amounts of gold extracted here are taken to the local buyers who melt the gold into buttons and pay the zamazamas out. The going rate is R340 a gram, well below the average world price which is around R440 per gram.

Devi Sankaree Govender: A 2007 report estimated that 10 percent of all gold mined in South Africa is stolen and makes its way onto the black market. But it’s not just local gold that feed syndicates.

Source 1: The first source are illegal gold that are coming in across the border. Mainly coming from Zim, Botswana, via South-West Africa, that’s coming in from Angola and the DRC.

This footage obtained by Carte Blanche shows illegal mining operations in Zimbabwe – the miners here, known as makorakoza, pan river beds for small amounts of gold. And like the abandoned mines in Springs, it’s hard and dangerous work.

(Anonymous Miner): Don’t move him you will damage his ribs. Just clear the shaft. The mineshaft collapsed, they were buried in the rubble.

But it’s not just the makorakoza who are supplying gold to the scam.

Source 1: So what’s happening in Zim at the moment, the majority of the mine owners only sell what they have to sell to the government to maintain their licenses. So all that extra gold gets smuggled across the border, comes into our country, gets sold to gold traders.

But what drives this trade? The high prices paid for gold in South Africa, where the smugglers, known as runners, can make up to 5 percent more than the world gold price.

Source 2: A lot of them would physically bring it through hidden in their cars. Obviously customs officials need to be paid, both on the Zimbabwean and South African side, so all the right individuals need to get paid to get it across the border.

5 kilograms of gold smuggled from Zimbabwe could easily have a street value of R2.3 million, and according to sources it’s not all that difficult to hide.

Source 1: The majority of the stuff coming across the border are small ingots, round ingots, if I would put a bunch of them together, an average male fist is about 4 to 5 kilos of those ingots.

In May, a Zimbabwean couple were caught trying to smuggle R6-million worth of gold through Beitbridge border post. Captain Paul Ramaloko of the Hawks says their attempts to stem the tide of smuggled gold is made more difficult by corrupt officials.

Captain Paul Ramaloko: We do have corrupt officials within a port of entry, either from the police service or from other law enforcement agencies, and it is through those members who relax on their ethics that these syndicates find their way to pursue their illegal activities.

(AD BREAK)

According to our sources, the illegal gold trade is so lucrative that upstanding members of the community are also getting involved.

Source 2: Teachers are doing gold deals on the school grounds, headmasters are becoming gold traders, they know you from school days they know you’re an idiot suddenly you’re a billionaire. If you can do it so can they.

Frans Styger is the headmaster of Hugenote High School, one the biggest schools in Springs. We heard he was one of the teachers involved in the gold trade. We found it hard to believe but decided to put it to the test.

Undercover Journalist: Ek het gehoor jy is ‘n man om met to praat as ek ‘n bietjie AU het om te skyf. (I heard you’re the man to speak to if I have some AU to move.)

Frans Styger (Principal Hugenote High School): Wat is dit? (What is that?)

Undercover Journalist: Goud. (Gold.)

Frans Styger: Oh, ja, jy kan… jy kan met my praat. (Oh, yes you can speak to me.)

We told Frans we had 1.475kgs of gold to sell. He seemed keen to help us as long as we cut him in on the deal.

Frans Styger: Ek het eintlik twee of drie ouens wat ek jou kan gee. (I actually have two or three guys I could give you.)

Undercover Journalist: Okay.

Frans Styger: Kom ons kyk of ons reg kom. (Let’s see if we come right.)

Undercover Journalist: Okay, nee, bakgat. (Okay, cool.)

Frans Styger: Hou dan maar net vir my ook ietsie uit, dan is dit fine. (Just keep a little something aside for me, then its fine.)

Buks and Cornelia Jansen sold Dedrego Refinery at the end of 2012. But our sources all claim Buks is still one of the major players in the industry. So we weren’t surprised when Frans revealed the name of his buyer.

Frans Styger: Kyk, die ou se naam is Buks Jansen. (Look the guy’s name is Buks Jansen.)

Undercover Journalist: Buks Jansen?

Frans Styger: Ja, hy het choppers en alles. (Ja, he has choppers and everything.)

Undercover Journalist: Hoe laat kan ek jou bel? (What time can I phone you?)

Frans Styger: Uh, dis saal opening en ek open die saal, dan is dit gebed, bel my so by tien uur, sodat ek die skool aan die gang het. (Uh, it’s assembly and I open assembly, and then it’s prayers, phone me at about ten, let me just get the school running.)

A few days later we called him again and he told us the deal would go down at his school.

Undercover Journalist: Sal jy saam met my gaan om die goed to gaan aflaai? (Will you go with me to drop the stuff off?)

Frans Styger: Dis by my skool. (It’s at my school.)

Undercover Journalist: Oh, is dit by jou skool? Oh, okay. (Oh, is it at your school. Okay.)

Frans Styger: Ja maar ek sien jou nie, jy laai dit net… as jy by die hek kom is die hout huisie aan die regter kant. Dit is sy wagte. Hy het ‘n wagte plek ook die ou. (Ja, but I don’t see you, you just drop it… if you come in the gate the wendyhouse is on the right there on your right hand side. It’s his guards. He has a guard company also this guy.)

Cornelia Jansen is the sole director of Safrane Security, the company providing guards at the Hugenote High School. Principal Styger told us to drop off the gold at Safrane’s guard house and pick up the cash the following day.

Frans Styger: Hy sal jou half ‘n miljoen gee, vyf hondred duisend rand se cash. As niemand sien wat niemand doen nie, dan kan niemand in die k*k kom. Ons wit mense moet nie mekaar spyker nie. (He’ll give you half a million, R500 000 in cash. If no one sees what anybody does, then no one gets in s**t. Because we white people shouldn’t nail each other.)

Devi Sankaree Govender: If the deal with Principal Frans Styger had gone through we would have arrived at the school and dropped off 1.475kg of illegal gold there, with the security. We then would have arrived a day later, and walked back out with R500 000 in cash.

Source 2: The Jansens are basically the police of Springs, Buks Jansen went as far a year ago as to say that he’s got more power than God in Springs. And unfortunately it’s not a wrong statement because he has.

Source 3: I’ll say it once more, I mean it’s all about money, everybody is in there for money, I think a lot of people have a price.

Devi Sankaree Govender: Once the syndicates have the illegal gold in their hands, they still have to get it into the legitimate system.

Source 3: The stuff comes in, we basically get the raw product, and then we need to alloy it down so we can declare it as jewellery.

Devi Sankaree Govender: The average 9 carat gold ring contains about 33 percent pure gold. But most black market gold ranges between 80 to 90 percent purity. So for the syndicates to make it seem as if the gold came from jewellery they have to add alloys, which believe it or not include brass padlocks and bullet casings to bring down the purity of that gold.

Source 2: So when I now present it to you I can convince you that it was jewellery at one stage.

Captain Paul Ramaloko (Hawks: Spokesperson): The syndicates will endeavour by all means to make sure they have clean hands at the end of the day.

Devi Sankaree Govender: The law on gold is very clear – gold bars, coins and nuggets are all zero rated, in other words you can’t add VAT when you sell it. But there’s a small loophole in the Second Hand Goods Act, which says that you can add VAT on gold jewellery and then claim the VAT back from SARS.

This is Adrian Lackay, spokesperson for the South African Revenue Services. After months of investigation, Carte Blanche approached SARS with our information. It turned out that SARS was not only aware of the scam but had been working hard to crack the same syndicates.

Adrian Lackay (SARS: Spokesperson): You must be able to show the origin of the product. You must have their physical address, their names, ID numbers and so on, and that’s where lots of the fraudulent activity happens because people steal IDs, they create a fake trail of paperwork, and that part of the operation is integral to this whole system of smuggling.

Source 1: Because remember your paperwork must be able to stand up against the scrutiny from a SARS audit when you’re audited.

The syndicates aren’t actually buying gold jewellery, so they need to forge truckloads of the necessary paperwork. Enter the Invoice Writers.

Source 1: Guys saw a gap in the market to start their own small little business. There’s numerous guys now where for anything between half a percent and a percent I can buy any volumes worth of paperwork that I want.

Adrian Lackay (SARS: Spokesperson): It’s a very lucrative current loophole that people are exploiting, they’ve identified it, they have created a whole criminal system that supports such activities.

One kilogram of illegal gold could require up to 700 invoices, and every invoice needs a copy of someone’s ID.

Source 1: The going rate at the moment is R50,000 for 10,000 IDs at Department of Home Affairs.

Source 2: So you would issue your ladies that doing the invoices each with 20,000 copies of IDs on average and she would sit and write out invoices piece by piece. I would give her a list and say “so many at 9ct, so many at 14 ct” and so forth. Now I’ve legitimized it completely.

Devi Sankaree Govender: That means that your ID, or even mine, could have been used in the scam, and we would never even know it.

The scam is so lucrative, and the need to move large volumes of gold so high, that the syndicates started looking elsewhere for their stock.

Source 3: A Krugerrand is the cheapest bullion you can buy. There’s no VAT on bullion.

Because you don’t pay VAT on Krugerrands, the syndicates can use the gold coins in the very same way they use black-market gold

Source 3: You just go buy the coins from whichever agent, you go home, you put it straight in the furnace, say bye-bye to Paul Kruger, and then you add a bit of silver and copper, take it down to the right percentage, and there you’re sitting with a piece of jewellery bar.

Then all they need is the invoice writers to produce the correct paperwork and…

Source 3:
You take it back to the refinery, that same gold that you just bought without VAT, take it back to the refinery, go sell it, and then you ask for VAT on it.

Most of the time when the syndicates buy Krugerrands or illegal gold from zamazamas, they’re paying more than the world gold price. But that doesn’t matter. Because once you’ve stolen the extra 14 percent VAT you’re still making a profit.

Devi Sankaree Govender: So with their paperwork in order and the gold alloyed down to the correct levels, the syndicates can then sell the gold to anyone they please.

We got hold of Cornelia Jansen to get her response to these allegations.

Cornelia Jansen (On the phone): You know what, I’m not involved so I don’t want to speak to you guys, sorry.

Devi Sankaree Govender: Do you have a number for Buks then for me?

Cornelia Jansen: He’s going to tell you the same

Devi Sankaree Govender: Can I speak to him so that it’s done, I don’t like other people doing my work.

Cornelia Jansen: (inaudible)

Devi Sankaree Govender: Sorry?

Cornelia Jansen: Well you know what he’s not with me at the moment.

Devi Sankaree Govender: Ja but do you have a cell number so that I can contact him?

Cornelia Jansen: But you don’t need to speak to him. We told you we are not in the business anymore, that’s it, and I’m not going to speak to you guys anymore. Please don’t phone me again. Thank you.

We have no valid telephone number for Buks Jansen, and so sent him written questions, but he hasn’t responded. Principal Frans Styger also denied being involved in the illegal gold trade.

Devi Sankaree Govender: You wanted to make arrangements for us to drop off the gold at your school, at your school. With your school security. What were you thinking? You’re a school principal, you operate a very well known school, and I’m not sure how people would feel, including the Department of Education, that you’re using the school to conduct illegal gold deals.

Frans Styger: No, no, no, it will not look good.

Devi Sankaree Govender: You deny it?

Frans Styger: Ja, ja, I deny it.

Devi Sankaree Govender: It’s highly organized and everybody along the chain makes money. But who loses out? It’s every South African.

Adrian says they have initiated 21 criminal cases against people involved in the scam, and they’re also going to court to try and get back some of the money being stolen.

Adrian Lackay (SARS: Spokesperson): At stake there’s about R1.007-billion that we have assessed for example outstanding taxes.

Despite the risks, the allure of the black-market trade seems hard to resist. And the key to the success of this scam seems to be frequent high turnover deals.

Source 3: And we can do it because we can do between 80 and 120 percent profit, especially if you turn your capital twice a day, three times a day. It’s possible, it’s been done before and it’s getting done now.

But there is hope on the horizon. SARS has made a submission to Parliament that could close the loophole in the Second Hand Goods Act that makes this entire scam possible.

Source 1: The only way they can do it to shut this industry down is gold sales in this country need to be zero-rated for VAT.

Adrian Lackay (SARS: Spokesperson): I think the current legislative proposals before parliament will have a significant impact, but that’s only from a revenue or a VAT perspective.

Meanwhile, the Hawks say the net is closing in on the illegal gold syndicates.

Captain Paul Ramaloko (Hawks: Spokesperson) If they haven’t heard from us yesterday, tomorrow or not long a distance we will be knocking on their doors.

Summary: Carte Blanche has done numerous stories about zamazamas and the illegal gold trade - it's costing the country in lives lost, violence in communities and gold stolen from legitimate mining operations. But what's fuelling this dangerous trade? Our investigation uncovers a complex gold scam that launders illegal gold while at the same time generating bogus VAT claims, resulting in billions of rands being stolen from SARS every year. We reveal how the scam works and who is profiting from the trade. Further information: A small loophole exists in the Second Hand Goods Act - all gold nuggets, ingots, bars and coins are zero-rated but gold jewellery isn't. It's this loophole that is fuelling the violent and dangerous illegal gold trade. Illegal gold traders on the ground are willing to pay over the world market price for gold. This creates an incentive to steal gold from legitimate mines, to mine gold illegally and to smuggle tonnes of gold into South Africa illegally. Once the gold is in South Africa it's sold on through a complex web of traders and refineries. Along the way the gold is melted down with other alloys to change what was pure gold into what looks strikingly similar to melted down jewellery. Paperwork is then forged to make it appear as if the gold did in fact come from second-hand jewellery buyers. With the gold disguised with other metals and with the correct paperwork the gold looks perfectly legitimate and is then sold on to the likes of Rand Refinery, local banks or exported. The end buyer has no idea that the gold they're buying may have been mined in dangerous underground illegal mines in South Africa, Zimbabwe, Angola or the DRC. We have three sources who agreed to interviews with their identities hidden - these sources have all been part of this illegal trade at one point or another. We have confirmed everything they have told us with members of the SARS task team on precious metals and with the Hawks. We have also been given Rand Refinery's internal figures for scrap gold purchases and Krugerrand sales which clearly demonstrate the extent of the problem. We also have undercover footage of illegal mining operations in Zimbabwe including two deaths that occurred on these mines. We also recorded phonecalls where we discussed doing an illegal gold deal with the principal of a high school in Springs. He specifically named his buyer - Buks Jansen. We believe we have enough evidence to implicate Buks as one of the major kingpins behind the illegal gold trade. We believe that through the refinery he used to own, Dedrego Trading, that he made false VAT claims fromnginto hundreds of millions of rands. Carte Blanche HD Nikola Vrahimis 23 January 2015 14 September 2014 - Carte Blanche HD Amalia Christoforou 06 November 2014 Press Release: Goldfinger In 1886 gold was discovered in Johannesburg, setting off a massive gold rush. More than a hundred years later, it would seem that very little has changed in the City of Gold. A new kind of randlord has emerged, dealing in gold on the black market. An ingenious scam that’s costing the country billions. Carte Blanche gets down to unearthing the facts. Script: FINAL SCRIPT: Goldfinger Date: 14 September 2014 Producer: Graham Coetzer Journalist: Susan Comrie Presenter: Devi Sankaree Govender Source 2 (Actor’s Voice / Identity Protected): You’re never going to stop the gold coming into the country – that we need to make peace with. Captain Paul Ramaloko (Hawks: Spokesperson): We are talking about serious money-laundering where millions are involved. Adrian Lackay (SARS: Spokesperson): They feed off the proceeds of crime, they literally partake in a system that sends poor, desperate people underground to illegally mine gold. Source 2: Teachers are doing gold deals on the school grounds, headmasters are becoming gold traders. Source 3 (Actor’s Voice / Identity Protected): And they’re portraying it like they’re this Christian people that does everything right. Source 1 (Actor’s Voice / Identity Protected): I was making ten million rand a month, by doing a thousand kilos a month, I was one of the biggest. Devi Sankaree Govender: This is Johannesburg’s East Rand, once one of the richest mining areas in the country. Although most of the mines have closed down, a new kind of “randlord” has emerged, buying up gold on the black market in an ingenious scam netting billions. This is Buks Jansen, a former cop from Springs who claims to have become an overnight millionaire by winning the lottery. But according to our sources he’s alleged to be one of the big five South African players in the illicit gold trade. Source 1: At the moment I would say Buks Jansen is one of the biggest guys left in the industry currently. This is Dedrego, a gold refinery in Springs that used to be run by Buks Jansen , although the company was registered in his wife Cornelia’s name. According to documents leaked to Carte Blanche, Dedrego did a turnover of R4 billion in 2011 and even considered taking a R100-million loan in order to finance more gold purchases. It is alleged that illegitimate as well as legitimate gold was refined here. Source 2: Everyone knows exactly what the Jansens are doing. But so many people is dependent on them that they just look the other way. Buks' alleged involvement in gold trading is part of a much wider network of organised crime syndicates involved in the illegal gold trade. It’s a sinister world where we are told that life is cheap and cash is king. Source 1: Even if I spend R10 million a month on security that will not be enough to protect me from the people involved in this industry. And here’s the big secret they’re all trying to protect – the illicit gold trade really has very little to do with the value of gold. The truth is the underground world of gold smuggling is actually fuelled by a massive VAT scam . Source 2: It’s just if you mine gold there’s no VAT to it, it’s a zero-rated item. The moment you sell second-hand gold jewellery, there’s a VAT to it It’s a complicated scam – but here’s a simplified example of how it works: • Step 1: The syndicates buy a R100 worth of illegal gold. Because it’s an illegal deal, they haven’t paid VAT on the R100. • Step 2: They employ an elaborate scheme to legitimise the illegal gold by claiming it comes from second-hand gold jewellery. • Step 3: Now they can sell the so-called legit gold again for a R100, but because they’re selling it through a registered VAT vendor, they are charging R114. Magically creating R14 profit. Source 2: According to government I have paid VAT therefore by law I’m allowed to get it back. In this case I never paid VAT I’m just purely stealing money out of the coffers of government. To really understand this scam we need to start at step 1, on the ground in Springs, a modern day gold boom town where syndicates are buying as much illegal gold as they can get their hands on. Devi Sankaree Govender: They’re called zamazamas which in isiZulu means “to try for just a little bit”. And that’s precisely what illegal miners in this area are doing – travelling down dangerous shafts and braving armed gunmen to get just a little bit of gold to sell on the black market. Chris Zulu: The zamazamas there is nothing more which they can do. They are looking for a job, they can’t find a job. They thought this is much better, where can they find something to eat, than to go to someone’s house and to go and break. This is Chris Zulu, he provides protection to a group of local zamazamas. Chris Zulu: Because there is a lot of fighting in these illegal minings. Shooting, killing each other. The mines in this area have all been closed and the shafts sealed, but illegal miners have found ways in. Contrary to popular belief, most zamazamas aren’t the people making the big money off illegal gold. Kenneth Dlamini (Sector 8 Community Policing Forum): Those zamazamas guys who go underground, they are only making something that they can live with. Kenneth Dlamini is a member of the Sector 8 Community Policing Forum but he also lives in Lindelani outside Springs, alongside many of the people involved in illegal mining. Kenneth Dlamini (Sector 8 Community Policing Forum): The bases here in Lindelani, there could be 20 to 30 bases, where they process their sand from the ground, because they go to different bases. The zamazamas we met were all Zimbabwean. They travel underground, about a kilometer down an abandoned ventilation shaft, where the zamazamas will often spend days mining in pitch darkness before returning to the surface. Once the gold has been brought to the surface, it’s taken to one of the many bases where the gold-bearing material is crushed and processed. Kenneth Dlamini (Sector 8 Community Policing Forum): They carry this bag from underground. They get it out like this. The material goes through two crushing processes, all done by hand. Kenneth Dlamini (Sector 8 Community Policing Forum): And after that, when it’s fine, they take it to the roller. The roller, or phenduka, is filled with steel ball-bearings and a mixture of water, mercury and cleaning detergents to get the mined material as fine as possible. Kenneth Dlamini (Sector 8 Community Policing Forum): The shiny thing it’s gold. The tiny amounts of gold extracted here are taken to the local buyers who melt the gold into buttons and pay the zamazamas out. The going rate is R340 a gram, well below the average world price which is around R440 per gram. Devi Sankaree Govender: A 2007 report estimated that 10 percent of all gold mined in South Africa is stolen and makes its way onto the black market. But it’s not just local gold that feed syndicates. Source 1: The first source are illegal gold that are coming in across the border. Mainly coming from Zim, Botswana, via South-West Africa, that’s coming in from Angola and the DRC. This footage obtained by Carte Blanche shows illegal mining operations in Zimbabwe – the miners here, known as makorakoza, pan river beds for small amounts of gold. And like the abandoned mines in Springs, it’s hard and dangerous work. (Anonymous Miner): Don’t move him you will damage his ribs. Just clear the shaft. The mineshaft collapsed, they were buried in the rubble. But it’s not just the makorakoza who are supplying gold to the scam. Source 1: So what’s happening in Zim at the moment, the majority of the mine owners only sell what they have to sell to the government to maintain their licenses. So all that extra gold gets smuggled across the border, comes into our country, gets sold to gold traders. But what drives this trade? The high prices paid for gold in South Africa, where the smugglers, known as runners, can make up to 5 percent more than the world gold price. Source 2: A lot of them would physically bring it through hidden in their cars. Obviously customs officials need to be paid, both on the Zimbabwean and South African side, so all the right individuals need to get paid to get it across the border. 5 kilograms of gold smuggled from Zimbabwe could easily have a street value of R2.3 million, and according to sources it’s not all that difficult to hide. Source 1: The majority of the stuff coming across the border are small ingots, round ingots, if I would put a bunch of them together, an average male fist is about 4 to 5 kilos of those ingots. In May, a Zimbabwean couple were caught trying to smuggle R6-million worth of gold through Beitbridge border post. Captain Paul Ramaloko of the Hawks says their attempts to stem the tide of smuggled gold is made more difficult by corrupt officials. Captain Paul Ramaloko: We do have corrupt officials within a port of entry, either from the police service or from other law enforcement agencies, and it is through those members who relax on their ethics that these syndicates find their way to pursue their illegal activities. (AD BREAK) According to our sources, the illegal gold trade is so lucrative that upstanding members of the community are also getting involved. Source 2: Teachers are doing gold deals on the school grounds, headmasters are becoming gold traders, they know you from school days they know you’re an idiot suddenly you’re a billionaire. If you can do it so can they. Frans Styger is the headmaster of Hugenote High School, one the biggest schools in Springs. We heard he was one of the teachers involved in the gold trade. We found it hard to believe but decided to put it to the test. Undercover Journalist: Ek het gehoor jy is ‘n man om met to praat as ek ‘n bietjie AU het om te skyf. (I heard you’re the man to speak to if I have some AU to move.) Frans Styger (Principal Hugenote High School): Wat is dit? (What is that?) Undercover Journalist: Goud. (Gold.) Frans Styger: Oh, ja, jy kan… jy kan met my praat. (Oh, yes you can speak to me.) We told Frans we had 1.475kgs of gold to sell. He seemed keen to help us as long as we cut him in on the deal. Frans Styger: Ek het eintlik twee of drie ouens wat ek jou kan gee. (I actually have two or three guys I could give you.) Undercover Journalist: Okay. Frans Styger: Kom ons kyk of ons reg kom. (Let’s see if we come right.) Undercover Journalist: Okay, nee, bakgat. (Okay, cool.) Frans Styger: Hou dan maar net vir my ook ietsie uit, dan is dit fine. (Just keep a little something aside for me, then its fine.) Buks and Cornelia Jansen sold Dedrego Refinery at the end of 2012. But our sources all claim Buks is still one of the major players in the industry. So we weren’t surprised when Frans revealed the name of his buyer. Frans Styger: Kyk, die ou se naam is Buks Jansen. (Look the guy’s name is Buks Jansen.) Undercover Journalist: Buks Jansen? Frans Styger: Ja, hy het choppers en alles. (Ja, he has choppers and everything.) Undercover Journalist: Hoe laat kan ek jou bel? (What time can I phone you?) Frans Styger: Uh, dis saal opening en ek open die saal, dan is dit gebed, bel my so by tien uur, sodat ek die skool aan die gang het. (Uh, it’s assembly and I open assembly, and then it’s prayers, phone me at about ten, let me just get the school running.) A few days later we called him again and he told us the deal would go down at his school. Undercover Journalist: Sal jy saam met my gaan om die goed to gaan aflaai? (Will you go with me to drop the stuff off?) Frans Styger: Dis by my skool. (It’s at my school.) Undercover Journalist: Oh, is dit by jou skool? Oh, okay. (Oh, is it at your school. Okay.) Frans Styger: Ja maar ek sien jou nie, jy laai dit net… as jy by die hek kom is die hout huisie aan die regter kant. Dit is sy wagte. Hy het ‘n wagte plek ook die ou. (Ja, but I don’t see you, you just drop it… if you come in the gate the wendyhouse is on the right there on your right hand side. It’s his guards. He has a guard company also this guy.) Cornelia Jansen is the sole director of Safrane Security, the company providing guards at the Hugenote High School. Principal Styger told us to drop off the gold at Safrane’s guard house and pick up the cash the following day. Frans Styger: Hy sal jou half ‘n miljoen gee, vyf hondred duisend rand se cash. As niemand sien wat niemand doen nie, dan kan niemand in die k*k kom. Ons wit mense moet nie mekaar spyker nie. (He’ll give you half a million, R500 000 in cash. If no one sees what anybody does, then no one gets in s**t. Because we white people shouldn’t nail each other.) Devi Sankaree Govender: If the deal with Principal Frans Styger had gone through we would have arrived at the school and dropped off 1.475kg of illegal gold there, with the security. We then would have arrived a day later, and walked back out with R500 000 in cash. Source 2: The Jansens are basically the police of Springs, Buks Jansen went as far a year ago as to say that he’s got more power than God in Springs. And unfortunately it’s not a wrong statement because he has. Source 3: I’ll say it once more, I mean it’s all about money, everybody is in there for money, I think a lot of people have a price. Devi Sankaree Govender: Once the syndicates have the illegal gold in their hands, they still have to get it into the legitimate system. Source 3: The stuff comes in, we basically get the raw product, and then we need to alloy it down so we can declare it as jewellery. Devi Sankaree Govender: The average 9 carat gold ring contains about 33 percent pure gold. But most black market gold ranges between 80 to 90 percent purity. So for the syndicates to make it seem as if the gold came from jewellery they have to add alloys, which believe it or not include brass padlocks and bullet casings to bring down the purity of that gold. Source 2: So when I now present it to you I can convince you that it was jewellery at one stage. Captain Paul Ramaloko (Hawks: Spokesperson): The syndicates will endeavour by all means to make sure they have clean hands at the end of the day. Devi Sankaree Govender: The law on gold is very clear – gold bars, coins and nuggets are all zero rated, in other words you can’t add VAT when you sell it. But there’s a small loophole in the Second Hand Goods Act, which says that you can add VAT on gold jewellery and then claim the VAT back from SARS. This is Adrian Lackay, spokesperson for the South African Revenue Services. After months of investigation, Carte Blanche approached SARS with our information. It turned out that SARS was not only aware of the scam but had been working hard to crack the same syndicates. Adrian Lackay (SARS: Spokesperson): You must be able to show the origin of the product. You must have their physical address, their names, ID numbers and so on, and that’s where lots of the fraudulent activity happens because people steal IDs, they create a fake trail of paperwork, and that part of the operation is integral to this whole system of smuggling. Source 1: Because remember your paperwork must be able to stand up against the scrutiny from a SARS audit when you’re audited. The syndicates aren’t actually buying gold jewellery, so they need to forge truckloads of the necessary paperwork. Enter the Invoice Writers. Source 1: Guys saw a gap in the market to start their own small little business. There’s numerous guys now where for anything between half a percent and a percent I can buy any volumes worth of paperwork that I want. Adrian Lackay (SARS: Spokesperson): It’s a very lucrative current loophole that people are exploiting, they’ve identified it, they have created a whole criminal system that supports such activities. One kilogram of illegal gold could require up to 700 invoices, and every invoice needs a copy of someone’s ID. Source 1: The going rate at the moment is R50,000 for 10,000 IDs at Department of Home Affairs. Source 2: So you would issue your ladies that doing the invoices each with 20,000 copies of IDs on average and she would sit and write out invoices piece by piece. I would give her a list and say “so many at 9ct, so many at 14 ct” and so forth. Now I’ve legitimized it completely. Devi Sankaree Govender: That means that your ID, or even mine, could have been used in the scam, and we would never even know it. The scam is so lucrative, and the need to move large volumes of gold so high, that the syndicates started looking elsewhere for their stock. Source 3: A Krugerrand is the cheapest bullion you can buy. There’s no VAT on bullion. Because you don’t pay VAT on Krugerrands, the syndicates can use the gold coins in the very same way they use black-market gold Source 3: You just go buy the coins from whichever agent, you go home, you put it straight in the furnace, say bye-bye to Paul Kruger, and then you add a bit of silver and copper, take it down to the right percentage, and there you’re sitting with a piece of jewellery bar. Then all they need is the invoice writers to produce the correct paperwork and… Source 3: You take it back to the refinery, that same gold that you just bought without VAT, take it back to the refinery, go sell it, and then you ask for VAT on it. Most of the time when the syndicates buy Krugerrands or illegal gold from zamazamas, they’re paying more than the world gold price. But that doesn’t matter. Because once you’ve stolen the extra 14 percent VAT you’re still making a profit. Devi Sankaree Govender: So with their paperwork in order and the gold alloyed down to the correct levels, the syndicates can then sell the gold to anyone they please. We got hold of Cornelia Jansen to get her response to these allegations. Cornelia Jansen (On the phone): You know what, I’m not involved so I don’t want to speak to you guys, sorry. Devi Sankaree Govender: Do you have a number for Buks then for me? Cornelia Jansen: He’s going to tell you the same Devi Sankaree Govender: Can I speak to him so that it’s done, I don’t like other people doing my work. Cornelia Jansen: (inaudible) Devi Sankaree Govender: Sorry? Cornelia Jansen: Well you know what he’s not with me at the moment. Devi Sankaree Govender: Ja but do you have a cell number so that I can contact him? Cornelia Jansen: But you don’t need to speak to him. We told you we are not in the business anymore, that’s it, and I’m not going to speak to you guys anymore. Please don’t phone me again. Thank you. We have no valid telephone number for Buks Jansen, and so sent him written questions, but he hasn’t responded. Principal Frans Styger also denied being involved in the illegal gold trade. Devi Sankaree Govender: You wanted to make arrangements for us to drop off the gold at your school, at your school. With your school security. What were you thinking? metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A new kind of randlord has emerged of Joburg's East rand, buying up illegally mined gold in an elaborate scam that's costing the country billions.
metadata.Summary: Carte Blanche has done numerous stories about zamazamas and the illegal gold trade - it's costing the country in lives lost, violence in communities and gold stolen from legitimate mining operations. But what's fuelling this dangerous trade? Our investigation uncovers a complex gold scam that launders illegal gold while at the same time generating bogus VAT claims, resulting in billions of rands being stolen from SARS every year. We reveal how the scam works and who is profiting from the trade.
metadata.Further information: A small loophole exists in the Second Hand Goods Act - all gold nuggets, ingots, bars and coins are zero-rated but gold jewellery isn't. It's this loophole that is fuelling the violent and dangerous illegal gold trade. Illegal gold traders on the ground are willing to pay over the world market price for gold. This creates an incentive to steal gold from legitimate mines, to mine gold illegally and to smuggle tonnes of gold into South Africa illegally. Once the gold is in South Africa it's sold on through a complex web of traders and refineries. Along the way the gold is melted down with other alloys to change what was pure gold into what looks strikingly similar to melted down jewellery. Paperwork is then forged to make it appear as if the gold did in fact come from second-hand jewellery buyers. With the gold disguised with other metals and with the correct paperwork the gold looks perfectly legitimate and is then sold on to the likes of Rand Refinery, local banks or exported. The end buyer has no idea that the gold they're buying may have been mined in dangerous underground illegal mines in South Africa, Zimbabwe, Angola or the DRC. We have three sources who agreed to interviews with their identities hidden - these sources have all been part of this illegal trade at one point or another. We have confirmed everything they have told us with members of the SARS task team on precious metals and with the Hawks. We have also been given Rand Refinery's internal figures for scrap gold purchases and Krugerrand sales which clearly demonstrate the extent of the problem. We also have undercover footage of illegal mining operations in Zimbabwe including two deaths that occurred on these mines. We also recorded phonecalls where we discussed doing an illegal gold deal with the principal of a high school in Springs. He specifically named his buyer - Buks Jansen. We believe we have enough evidence to implicate Buks as one of the major kingpins behind the illegal gold trade. We believe that through the refinery he used to own, Dedrego Trading, that he made false VAT claims fromnginto hundreds of millions of rands.
